classes.term: the removal of embedded metadata from image files in sharing and transit (what the tests measure)
classes.basis: field: B13 (IPTC Photo Metadata Research: 'when they shared photos via social media sites or systems, their embedded metadata disappeared'; 'to understand how image sharing, through upload and download, affects the integrity of embedded metadata'); B12 (2019 results: 'metadata is stripped off in SavedAs or downloaded files'); B4 (User Guide: 'may be stripping out embedded metadata fields'); B9 (FAQ: 'the metadata might be stripped from your images by some software on your site')

classes.term: embedded image metadata (Exif, IPTC IIM and XMP inside the file) as provenance carrier (what the tests test)
classes.basis: field: B12 (2019 results, test procedure: 'are the embedded Exif and IPTC metadata (in the formats IIM and XMP) of the uploaded image still embedded?'); B2 (the Standard: 'IPTC worked alongside Adobe on the technical implementation of the metadata that employs Adobe's XMP technology'); census provenance_carrier 'embedded metadata inside the image file' (PE)

config.classes_note: Two classes, each sourced from the field by locus, and kept apart because the address names one object and the record another: (1) the removal of embedded metadata in sharing and transit, which is what the tests measure (B13, B12, B4, B9); (2) embedded image metadata as a provenance carrier, which is what the tests test (B12, B2; the census's provenance_carrier). The census's own lineage and kind for the entity are 'media' and 'test series' (census.json rows[slug == 'iptc-photo-metadata-tests'], lineage, kind); neither is a string the archive uses of other things, so they are not run as classes. Aliases: the operator's abbreviation and full name (a string candidate on 'IPTC' bears on the operator or the standard and is admitted at D only where the tests are named; a claim the archive makes on the standard is read at O-class 2, the carrier, and composed as a claim on the carrier, never as a claim on the tests), the Working Group and the tests' page names, the Embedded Metadata Manifesto the User Guide endorses, the IPTC's Metawatch (the census's successor in method) and GetPMD, and the domain. Admission by reading (§3.4): a sentence or paragraph that makes a claim on the tests, on embedded metadata's survival in transit, or applies an archive category (provenance erasure, PER, scaffold, Layer 1 metadata, survival) to either class; a bibliography line, a checklist or a field map of the archive's own files is not a claim on the class.
